verdict.rationale: Gmail's own filters evaluate incoming mail by sender, subject or size and automatically apply labels, so a user can route mail into labeled streams. Search operators can be turned into filters. The evidence does not show a split or tabbed inbox view, automatic importance ranking, or calendar-invite detection, so priority-ordered triage is only approximated with manual rules. Missing for 10: a documented split-inbox/category view, automatic importance-based prioritization, built-in streams for newsletters/team/calendar invites, hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can split my inbox into focused streams — important, team, newsletters, calendar invites — so triage happens in priority order, not arrival order

citations.quote: When a message matches, filters automatically trigger actions such as adding or removing labels, or forwarding the email to a specified address.
Advanced rules configured for an account that evaluate incoming messages against specific matching criteria (like sender, subject, or size).
After you search, you can use the results to set up a filter for these messages.
